option.name: text
option.value: This is an educational Android project called Howest Desserts. Package: be.howest.henrique.howestdesserts. Use Kotlin. Use Jetpack Compose. Do not create XML layouts. Prefer simple, readable code for students new to Android. Do not add a library without first explaining why it is required. Use the existing Gradle version catalog. Use a ViewModel as the screen-level state holder. Expose screen state with StateFlow. Prefer state down and events up. Do not add Retrofit, Room or Navigation. Do not introduce repositories, dependency injection or a domain layer. Explain significant generated code. Do not modify unrelated files.

option.name: text
option.value:
Create a Kotlin data class Dessert that matches this JSON object: {"id": 0, "productName": "Cupcake", "imageFile": "https://...", "description": "...", "size": 500, "price": 5.0}. Explain each field and why a data class is used.
Which dependencies do I need for Coil AsyncImage with remote image URLs, viewModel() in Compose and collectAsStateWithLifecycle()? Explain why each one is required and how to add them to the version catalog.
Create a DessertViewModel and a DessertUiState that expose a hardcoded List<Dessert> using StateFlow. Explain the difference between MutableStateFlow and StateFlow.
Create a DessertRoute composable that collects the ui state with collectAsStateWithLifecycle() and passes the desserts to a stateless DessertListScreen. Explain what “state down, events up” means here.
Create a reusable Material 3 DessertCard with Coil AsyncImage that shows the image, product name, stock and price, and a DessertListScreen with a two-column LazyVerticalGrid.
Create a reusable, stateless DessertDetailScreen that shows one Dessert: image, product name, description, size and price. Add a @Preview. Do not use Navigation Compose.
Explain this Kotlin error: “Argument type mismatch: actual type is ‘String’, but ‘Int’ was expected” when creating a data class instance.

option.name: text
option.value:
Add Retrofit and the Gson converter to the version catalog and app/build.gradle.kts. Explain why each library is needed. Do not change anything else.
Create a DessertDto that matches the JSON of the Flask API and a toDessert() mapping function to the existing Dessert model. Explain why a DTO is separate from the UI model.
Create a Retrofit DessertApiService for GET /desserts and GET /desserts/{id}, and a DessertRepository that receives the service as a constructor parameter and maps DessertDto to Dessert.
Change DessertUiState into a sealed interface with Loading, Success and Error, and update DessertRoute so it shows a loading screen, the dessert list or an error screen with a retry button.
Change DessertViewModel to receive DessertRepository as a constructor dependency. Create an AppContainer that builds Retrofit and the repository once, and a custom DessertApplication class. Explain why Retrofit should not be created inside the ViewModel.
AppContainer does not compile: "Cannot infer type for type parameter 'T'" and unresolved DessertApiService and DessertRepository. Explain the cause and fix it without changing unrelated files.
Allow cleartext HTTP only to 10.0.2.2 for the local Flask API using a network security config. Explain why this is a development-only exception and what must change before publishing.
Add Room (runtime, ktx, compiler) and the KSP plugin to the version catalog and Gradle files. Explain why each is required. This project uses AGP 9 with built-in Kotlin.
The build fails with "Using kotlin.sourceSets DSL to add Kotlin sources is not allowed with built-in Kotlin" and the previews still use the deleted DessertData. Explain the cause and fix both.
Create a Room CartItemEntity, a CartDao with a Flow for all items, and a CartDatabase for the local shopping cart only. Do not store the dessert list in Room. Explain each annotation.
Create a CartRepository separate from DessertRepository that maps CartItemEntity to a CartItem model, and create the Room database once in AppContainer using the application context.
Create CartUiState, a CartViewModel exposing a StateFlow built from the Room Flow, and a reusable CartRoute and stateless CartScreen matching the provided cart mock-up.
Add Navigation Compose to the version catalog and app/build.gradle.kts. Explain why it is required. Use string routes, no kotlinx.serialization plugin.
Add a Navigation Compose NavHost with bottom navigation for Desserts and Cart. Desserts is a nested graph so a detail screen can be its child. Use string routes.
Navigate from the dessert list to a detail destination inside the Desserts graph, passing only the dessert ID. Load the dessert in a DessertDetailViewModel using SavedStateHandle, add an Up button and an Add to cart action through CartRepository. Keep DessertDetailScreen stateless.
Add a Share cart action to the cart screen using an implicit Intent with ACTION_SEND, text/plain, the cart summary in EXTRA_TEXT and the Android chooser. Do not request permissions and do not share the database file.
Trace the two data paths in this project: Flask → Retrofit → DessertRepository → DessertViewModel → StateFlow → Compose, and Room → CartDao → CartRepository → CartViewModel → StateFlow → Compose. For every external dependency, explain why it is part of the application.
